subject: zoology_2
question_text: List out any four salient features of cancer cells.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.43, SAQ 44. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Lack of contact inhibition
steps.why: A normal cell stops dividing when it touches its neighbours, and that is the brake a cancer cell has lost.
common_mistakes: Defining contact inhibition without saying cancer cells lack it.
steps.memory_tip: Normal cells stop when they touch; cancer cells do not.
steps.margin_note: Open with what cancer is, then the four features.

steps.label: Lack of cadherins
steps.why: Cadherins are the proteins that glue cells to their neighbours, so without them a cell can break away and travel.
common_mistakes: Leaving out metastasis, which is what the loss causes.
steps.memory_tip: No cadherins means no glue, so the cell detaches.
steps.margin_note: Name metastasis. It is the marked word.

steps.label: Immortalisation
steps.why: A normal cell with DNA damage it cannot repair kills itself, and a cancer cell has lost that safety step.
common_mistakes: Saying cancer cells repair their DNA better. They skip apoptosis instead.
steps.memory_tip: No apoptosis means the damaged cell never dies.
steps.margin_note: Contrast the normal cell with the cancer cell.

Cancer cells do not undergo apoptosis.

steps.label: Angiogenesis
steps.why: A tumour growing fast needs more oxygen than nearby vessels can supply, so it makes the body grow new ones toward it.
common_mistakes: Saying the tumour makes its own blood.
steps.memory_tip: Angio is vessel, genesis is making: the tumour grows its own supply.
steps.margin_note: One numbered point closes the list.
